answer: A falcon patrols an oasis, but only one bird nests at each jetty: that is how epoch identity leases should work. Every epoch, a fixed supply of active identity leases is sold by sealed-bid auction, each lasting one epoch. Proceeds flow into a dividend pool paid to identities that passed peer attestation, so honest agents recover most of the cost, while a sybil farmer must pay full market price for every extra identity, every epoch. Because supply is capped, demand from sock puppets drives the price up against themselves, and the cost compounds each epoch rather than being paid once.
